lessons.title: ¡Hola!
lessons.tip: Greetings follow the clock: buenos días (morning), buenas tardes (afternoon), buenas noches (night). Días is masculine, tardes and noches are feminine, so the ending changes.

lessons.title: Words you already know

sentences.target: El aeropuerto, el banco, el hospital.
sentences.english: The airport, the bank, the hospital.

lines.target: Bien, gracias. El taxi, por favor.

lessons.tip: Every noun is el (masculine) or la (feminine). Words ending in -o are usually el (el banco), -a usually la (la música). Learn the el/la together with the word.

lessons.title: Who I am

items.english: pleased to meet you (said by a man)

sentences.english: I'm Luis. Nice to meet you.
How are you? Very well, and you?

lines.english: My name is Tom. And you?
My name is Ana. Nice to meet you.

lessons.tip: me llamo = "I'm called" (your name); soy = "I am". The yo is optional: Soy Tom = Yo soy Tom. A man says encantado, a woman says encantada.

lessons.title: Where I'm from

sentences.english: I'm from England. I speak English.
Do you speak Spanish? — A little.

sentences.target: No entiendo. Más despacio, por favor.

sentences.english: Once more, please. What does "ciudad" mean?
How do you say "city"? — La ciudad.

lines.english: I'm from Spain. Do you speak Spanish?

replyOptions: Un poco. Más despacio, por favor.

lessons.tip: Soy de + place = "I'm from"; hablo + language = "I speak". The verb ending shows who: hablo (I speak), hablas (you speak).

lessons.title: Yes, no, maybe

sentences.english: Do you speak English? — Yes, of course.

lines.english: Excuse me, do you speak English?

lessons.tip: Keep short answers in your pocket: sí, no, claro, está bien. No pasa nada = "nothing happens" = no worries. ¿Qué? / ¿Cómo? are your "pardon?" when you miss something.

lessons.title: Coffee & drinks

sentences.target: El café con leche, por favor.
La cerveza y el vino, por favor.
sentences.english: The beer and the wine, please.

sentences.target: Soy Tom. El vaso, por favor.

lines.target: Bien, gracias. El café, por favor.

lessons.tip: con = with, sin = without: café con leche, agua sin hielo. Careful: el agua is feminine even though it says el (la agua would sound clumsy).

lessons.title: Food basics

sentences.target: La pizza con queso, por favor.
El pollo con arroz, por favor.
El café con leche y el pan, por favor.
sentences.english: The coffee with milk and the bread, please.

lines.target: Bien, gracias. La sopa, por favor.

lessons.tip: Cognates are free: la sopa, la ensalada, la pizza, la fruta, la pasta are almost English. Always learn the el/la with the word.

lessons.title: I'd like…

example.english: Can I have the water, please?

example.target: Para mí, la pizza, por favor.

sentences.english: Can I have the water, please?
The menu, please. What do you recommend?

sentences.target: Para mí, la pizza para llevar. Nada más.
sentences.english: For me, the pizza to go. Nothing else.

sentences.target: ¿Algo más? — No, la cuenta, por favor.
sentences.english: Anything else? — No, the bill, please.

fills.english: Can I have the water, please?

lines.english: Good, thanks. What do you recommend?
The pizza with cheese. Anything else?

lessons.tip: Quiero = "I want" (direct), quisiera = "I'd like" (polite). To ask in a bar or shop: ¿Me das…? in Latin America, ¿Me pones…? in Spain.

lessons.title: Tapas & tacos

sentences.target: El jamón y el chorizo, gracias.
sentences.english: The ham and the chorizo, thanks.

sentences.target: Para mí, la paella y las aceitunas.
sentences.english: For me, the paella and the olives.

lessons.tip: Plural: add -s, and el/la become los/las: el taco → los tacos, la tapa → las tapas. Heads-up: "tortilla" is a flat bread in Mexico but an omelette in Spain, and fries are papas fritas (Spain: patatas fritas).

lessons.title: Eating & drinking

sentences.target: Tengo sed. El agua, por favor.
El jugo está frío y dulce.
sentences.english: The juice is cold and sweet.
sentences.spain: El zumo está frío y dulce.

lines.english: The soup is hot. Enjoy your meal!

lessons.tip: Está + adjective = how something is right now: está caliente, está rico. Tengo + hambre/sed = "I have hunger/thirst" = I'm hungry/thirsty. Buen provecho = "enjoy your meal".

lessons.title: Zero to eleven

sentences.english: Ten tacos and eleven tapas, thanks!

lines.target: Bien, gracias. Dos tacos, por favor.

lessons.tip: Learn numbers as sounds, not spellings. Cero is zero; uno shortens to un before a masculine noun (un café), but in a count you just say uno, dos, tres.

lessons.title: Twelve to a hundred

lines.target: Bien, gracias. Doce tacos, por favor.

lines.english: Twelve? What an appetite! With salsa?

lessons.tip: 16 to 29 glue into one word (dieciséis, veintiuno), and the accent matters. From 31 on it is three words: treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos.

lessons.title: Big numbers

sentences.english: Two hundred, five hundred, a thousand.

sentences.target: El primero, el segundo, el tercero.
sentences.english: The first, the second, the third.

fills.english: Two hundred, five hundred, a thousand.

lines.target: Setenta y ocho, noventa y nueve.
Setenta y ocho, noventa y nueve. ¿Está bien?

lessons.tip: Hundreds are one word: doscientos, quinientos. Mil = 1,000, never "un mil"; un millón = 1,000,000. Primero, segundo, tercero, último = 1st, 2nd, 3rd, last.

lessons.title: Prices

example.english: How much does the coffee cost?

sentences.english: How much does the coffee cost?
How much is it? — Twenty dollars.

sentences.target: Está muy caro. El precio, por favor.
sentences.english: It's very expensive. The price, please.
Free? How nice! I have the card.

fills.english: How much does the coffee cost?

lessons.tip: ¿Cuánto cuesta? = how much does it cost (one thing); ¿Cuánto es? = how much is it (the total). Money words are cognates: el euro, el dólar, el peso.

lessons.title: Paying

example.english: I want to pay in cash.

sentences.english: Do you take cards? — Yes, of course.
I want to pay in cash.

sentences.target: El cambio y el recibo, por favor.
sentences.english: The change and the receipt, please.
Do you charge a tip? — I don't know.

sentences.target: Quiero sacar dinero. La factura, gracias.
sentences.english: I want to withdraw money. The invoice, thanks.

fills.english: I want to pay in cash.

lessons.tip: Words ending in -ción are nearly free (la información, la conversación). Pagar = to pay, and after quiero the verb stays in the infinitive: quiero pagar, quiero sacar dinero.

lessons.title: Where is…?

sentences.target: El banco está allí, a la derecha.
sentences.english: The bank is there, on the right.

sentences.target: La calle, a la izquierda. La esquina, allí.
sentences.english: The street, on the left. The corner, there.

fills.english: The bank is on the right.

lines.target: Está allí, todo derecho. No está lejos.
lines.english: It's there, straight ahead. It's not far.

lessons.tip: ¿Dónde está…? works for anything. Add aquí/allí (here/there) and cerca/lejos (near/far). Latin America says todo derecho and ¿Dónde queda…?; Spain says todo recto and just ¿Dónde está…?.

lessons.title: Transport

example.english: The gas station, on the right.

sentences.target: Quiero el tren. La estación está aquí.
sentences.english: I want the train. The station is here.

lines.english: Excuse me, where is the stop?

lessons.tip: -ción = -tion: la estación is "station". Transport words are mostly cognates (el metro, la bicicleta). Latin America says el carro and el boleto; Spain says el coche and el billete.

lessons.title: Asking directions

example.english: How do I get to the square?
I want to go to the beach.
I want to cross the street.

sentences.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
I'm lost. Where is the map?
I'm going to the square. How long does it take?
I want to cross the street.

sentences.target: Doblar a la derecha, todo derecho.
sentences.spain: Girar a la derecha, todo recto.

fills.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the square?

lines.target: Disculpe, estoy perdido. ¿Cómo llego a la estación?
lines.english: Excuse me, I'm lost. How do I get to the station?

lines.target: Todo derecho y a la izquierda. No está lejos.
lines.english: Straight ahead and to the left. It's not far.

lessons.tip: voy a + place = "I'm going to" (Voy a la plaza). Verbs like ir, llegar, seguir, cruzar are infinitives, and after quiero they never change. Spain prefers girar to doblar.

lessons.title: Places in town

example.english: I want to go to the beach.

sentences.english: I want to go to the beach.

sentences.target: El museo, la iglesia, el parque.
sentences.english: The museum, the church, the park.

sentences.target: La universidad, la oficina y el mercado, todo derecho.
sentences.english: The university, the office and the market, straight ahead.
sentences.spain: La universidad, la oficina y el mercado, todo recto.

fills.english: I want to go to the beach.

lines.english: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?

lines.target: Está allí, a la derecha. Cerca.
lines.english: It's there, on the right. Near.

lessons.tip: -dad = -ty: la universidad, la nacionalidad, la realidad. Place words are nearly all cognates (el museo, el parque, la farmacia). Spain says el servicio (or los aseos) for the toilet.

lessons.title: Asking for help

example.english: Excuse me, can you help me?
What time does the train leave?

sentences.english: Excuse me, can you help me?
What time does the train leave?

sentences.target: El museo está abierto, el banco está cerrado.
sentences.english: The museum is open, the bank is closed.

sentences.target: La entrada está a la izquierda. La fila, allí.
sentences.english: The entrance is on the left. The line, there.
sentences.spain: La entrada está a la izquierda. La cola, allí.

fills.english: What time does the train leave?

lines.english: Excuse me, can you help me?

replyOptions: Gracias. ¿A qué hora sale el tren?

lessons.tip: ¿Me puede ayudar? is the polite magic phrase: it uses the usted form (puede) for strangers, shop staff and officials. ¡Ayuda! and ¡Cuidado! are for emergencies. Spain says la cola for the queue.

units.title: I want / I have / I need

lessons.title: I want

example.english: I want to go to the beach.
I want to see the museum.
I can't wait for the paella!

sentences.english: I want to eat. I'm hungry.
What do you want? Do you want coffee?
I want to go to the beach.
I want to speak Spanish. I want more.

lines.english: I'm hungry. I want to eat.

lessons.tip: quiero + infinitive: quiero comer, quiero ir. The verb after quiero never changes. No quiero = "I don't want". ¿Quieres…? = "do you want…?" (to a friend).

lessons.title: I have

sentences.target: Tengo un problema. No tengo dinero.
sentences.english: I have a problem. I don't have money.
I'm in a hurry. See you later!
I'm cold. I want hot coffee.

sentences.target: Tengo calor. Quiero agua con hielo.
sentences.english: I'm hot. I want water with ice.

sentences.target: Tengo sueño. Tengo ganas de ir al hotel.
sentences.english: I'm sleepy. I feel like going to the hotel.

lines.english: I'm in a hurry. Do you have time?

lines.target: Lo siento. No tengo tiempo. ¡Hasta luego!
lines.english: Sorry. I don't have time. See you later!

lessons.tip: Spanish "has" feelings: tengo frío (I have cold) = I'm cold, and the same for hambre, sed, sueño, prisa, miedo. Never "soy frío" (that means "I am a cold person"). Tengo ganas de + verb = "I feel like…".

lessons.title: I need

sentences.target: Necesito un taxi. ¿Dónde está la parada?
sentences.english: I need a taxi. Where is the stop?
I'm sleepy. I need to sleep.
Do you need anything? — No, I don't need anything.

fills.english: I'm sleepy. I need to sleep.

lines.english: I have a problem. I need help.
One moment. Do you need a doctor?

lessons.tip: necesito + noun or verb, just like quiero: necesito agua, necesito dormir. Un = "a" before a masculine noun (un taxi, un médico). Spain says el servicio for the toilet.

lessons.title: Is / is it

sentences.target: Esto es el hotel. Eso es la estación.
sentences.english: This is the hotel. That is the station.

sentences.target: Es verdad. El español es fácil.

sentences.english: I'm tired. I need to sleep.
I'm ready. Is the coffee ready?

lines.english: I'm tired. I need to sleep.
Are you ready? The taxi is here.

lessons.tip: es = what something is or generally like (es fácil, es verdad); está / estoy = state or place (está aquí, estoy cansado). Learn each as a chunk and don't overthink the difference yet.

lessons.title: Question words

example.english: How many tacos do you want?

sentences.english: Which one do you want? — I want that.
How many tacos do you want?
Can I pay by card? Is that allowed?

sentences.target: ¿A dónde? Voy a la playa. ¿Con quién?
sentences.english: Where to? I'm going to the beach. With whom?

fills.english: How many tacos do you want?

lines.target: Voy a la playa mañana. ¿Quieres ir?
lines.english: I'm going to the beach tomorrow. Do you want to come?

lessons.tip: Question words always carry an accent (quién, cuándo, dónde, cuál, cuánto) and a question starts with ¿. ¿Puedo…? = "may I…?"; ¿Se puede…? = "is it allowed / possible to…?".
